claims.statement: For finite bipartite H with alpha(H)<=h, marked set W and 1<=k<=h, the stated exact marked incidence identity holds with D,C>=0. In the ordinary-tree specialization, each selected original leaf tag contributes q_v(k+1)-q_v(k), so the complete selected sum equals the sum of these tagged differences.
claims.scope: Exact finite bipartite incidence identity and its application to each selected original leaf of an eligible lower-region ordinary tree, retaining distinct tags for leaves with common support.
claims.reason: retained: The addability bound and incidence pair count prove the identity directly. The tree domain, alpha(H)=alpha(T)-1, 1<=k<=h, fixed selector and rank shift give the exact summand identity. This is an algebraic reformulation and does not prove the aggregate sign.

claims.statement: The primary target is exactly the selected aggregate inequality sum_F q_v(k+1)<=sum_F q_v(k). An injection within each component of the disjoint union of per-tag incidence graphs is only sufficient and is too strong to hold universally: the T22 and T60 controls have a positive tag despite a negative complete sum. No proof of the aggregate inequality or eligible positive witness is established.
claims.scope: The fixed favorable selector F(T,p) in the exact lower-region ordinary-tree target; control obstruction to the proposed tagwise matching condition at T22 and T60 only.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: The exact shadow reformulation leaves the target inequality unchanged. Positive summands in the standing controls prevent an upper-to-lower injection componentwise by tag, while their full sums remain negative. A cross-tag matching would require a new incidence rule and proof; none is supplied.

limitations: The global selected marked-shadow inequality remains unproved, and no eligible ordinary-tree counterexample is established.
The exact incidence identity is an equivalent reformulation of each summand and supplies no independent sign estimate.
T22 and T60 control rows were re-summed from pinned JSON copies; their graph generation and tree-DP computations were not independently rerun.
The K_(1,12) check is one finite control only; no exhaustive tree search or literature theorem was used.
